//: Reviewed co-occurrences: a Best-practice row reading NOT MET on a document whose SAME category carries a failing WCAG criterion. Each entry means a person confirmed the row is about a different defect than the failure. Regenerate with `pnpm best-practice-basis --bless` and fill in `reviewed` in the same commit.

pairs.reviewed: Different defects in the same category. The SCORED failures are about WHERE the text is: a structure tree that references no content, and 24,697 characters painted outside the tagged content entirely, so nothing a screen reader follows reaches them (1.3.1). This row is about whether characters can be DECODED to readable text at all — a broken or absent ToUnicode map, which is a PDF/UA concern and unscored below the small band. A document can have perfectly mapped characters that are entirely untagged (this one), or fully tagged text that extracts as garbage. Neither implies the other. Reviewed 2026-08-31 on Drug Testing Lit Review.

Different defects in the same category. The SCORED failure is structural — 8 link annotations sit on the page with no <Link> element wrapping them, so a screen reader following the tag tree never reaches them at all (1.3.1). This row is about the WORDING of link text, which is unscored because WCAG 2.4.4 lets the surrounding sentence supply a link's purpose and no text-only check can weigh that. The two are independent: a perfectly tagged link can read "click here", and an untagged link can carry excellent text. Fixing one does not fix the other. Reviewed 2026-08-31 on 2025_Death_in_Custody_FINAL.

Different defects. 3.1.1 Language of Page fails because the document declares no language (or a meaningless one); this row is about the DisplayDocTitle viewer preference. Neither touches the other: a file can declare en-US perfectly and still show its filename in the title bar.

Different defects. The 1.3.1 failure in text_extractability is untagged visible content or unmappable characters past the scored threshold; this row is about whether a font's glyph program ships inside the file. Assistive technology reads the encoding, not the embedded outlines, so embedding is a print-fidelity matter.

Different defects. The 1.3.1 failure in reading_order comes from list or structure defects the analyzer confirms; this row is about unique /ID values on <Note> elements, which PDF/UA 7.9 asks for and WCAG does not. The reference-to-note association is carried by the matching visible numerals and the link annotation.

Same category, adjacent properties — deliberately separated. The scored 1.3.1 failure is a malformed list (missing <LBody>, so list structure is not determinable). This row is only about <Lbl>, the bullet or number marker, which ISO 32000 makes optional and whose absence leaves the list structure intact. Both can be true of one list; the row must not read as absolution for the list as a whole.

Different defects. The scored 1.3.1 failure in link_quality is a link with no tag around it, so no link relationship exists to expose; this row is about the wording of a link that IS tagged. A raw URL satisfies 2.4.4 Level A on its own terms.

Different defects, and different questions. The scored 1.3.1 failure is a confirmed structure defect; this row is a heuristic comparison of tag order against draw order, which fails nothing by itself — a correctly remediated document routinely diverges from paint order on purpose.

Different defects. The scored 1.3.1 failure is a COMPLEX table (headers on more than one edge, or spanned cells) with neither /Scope nor /Headers, which conformance.ts asserts explicitly. This row is about SIMPLE tables — headers along one edge, nothing spanned — where position alone makes the relationship determinable, so PDF/UA asks for /Scope and WCAG does not.
